scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You drop a cheque in the bank box, and in a day or so the money arrives. Does the paper travel to the other bank?

scenes.name: cts
scenes.text: Not anymore. India uses CTS, the cheque truncation system. The paper journey is cut short.

scenes.name: scan
scenes.text: Your bank scans the cheque, capturing images of the front and back, plus the data in the code line.

scenes.name: clearing
scenes.text: The images and data are sent electronically to a clearing house, which passes them to the payer's bank.

scenes.name: check
scenes.text: The payer's bank checks the signature, the balance and the details, then accepts or returns it.

scenes.name: positive
scenes.text: For large cheques, positive pay lets the payer confirm details in advance, to catch fraud.

scenes.name: credit
scenes.text: Once accepted, money is settled between banks and credited to you, usually within a working day or so.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Scan, send, check, settle. The image travels, not the paper. Follow for more on how things really work.
